svg.title: Two triangles with the same two angle measures and one 5-unit side, placed differently
svg.desc: Two independently drawn noncongruent triangles each have angle A equal to 40 degrees and angle B equal to 60 degrees, so the third angle C is 80 degrees. In the first triangle AB equals 5 units, the side between the marked angles. In the second triangle AC equals 5 units instead, across from the 60 degree angle, while AB is about 5.686 units. The matching numerical data of 40 degrees, 60 degrees and length 5 do not describe the same triangle unless the location of the 5-unit side is also matched. Rotating or reflecting a triangle without changing corresponding measurements gives an identical copy; changing which labeled side has length 5 does not. These are original Edulytiks coordinate figures, not source publisher graphics.
svg.text: Which side is the length 5? Position matters.
The 5-unit side joins the 40° and 60° vertices.
The 5-unit side now joins the 40° and 80° vertices.
First-party comparison: match corresponding sides and angles, then justify whether figures overlay.
